messages.content:
You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: By which date must Member States provide for the first time the data and information referred to in Article 6(5) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230?

Passages:
[0] REG, Art. 53(3) — rank: law — corrected by the corrigendum (Corrigendum, point 9: '14 July 2026' now reads '20 July 2026')
Article 53 Evaluation and review. 3. By 20 July 2026 and every five years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a specific report on the assessment of Article 6(4) and (5) of this Regulation to the European Parliament and to the Council. The reports shall be made public. The Commission shall include in its reports the following: (a) a summary of data and information provided by Member States in accordance with Article 6(5) during the reporting period; (b) an assessment of the list of categories of machinery or related products in Annex I in view of the criteria set out in Article 6(4). In the reports, the Commission shall assess the appropriateness and availability of data and information provided by Member States, including its sufficiency and suitability for the purposes of making comparisons, identifying any shortcomings, necessary to ensure effective functioning and enforcement of Article 6.

[1] eu-dir-2012-18, Art. 21(2) — rank: law
Article 21 Information system and exchanges. 2. By 30 September 2019, and every four years thereafter, Member States shall provide the Commission with a report on the implementation of this Directive.

[2] REG, Art. 6(9) — rank: law — corrected by the corrigendum (Corrigendum, point 1: '14 July 2025' now reads '20 July 2025')
Article 6 Categories of machinery and related products listed in Annex I subject to relevant conformity assessment procedures. 9. By 20 July 2025, and every five years thereafter, Member States shall provide the data and information referred to in paragraph 5, including information to the effect that none of the events referred to in paragraph 5 has occurred, for every category of machinery or related products which is included in Annex I or which is not included in Annex I where that non-inclusion is a cause of concern for the Member State.

[3] eu-reg-2023-988, Art. 24(1) — rank: law
Article 24 Reporting. 1. Member States shall communicate to the Commission, not later than two years after the adoption of the implementing act referred to in paragraph 2 and every year thereafter, data concerning the application of this Regulation. Following the communication from the Member States, the Commission shall draw up annually a summary report and make it available to the public.

[4] eu-dir-2009-104, Recital 10 — rank: law
(10) Pursuant to Directive 98/34/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 June 1998 laying down a procedure for the provision of information in the field of technical standards and regulations and of rules on Information Society services ( 6 ) , Member States are required to notify the Commission of any draft technical regulations relating to machines, equipment and installations.

[5] eu-reg-2023-988, Art. 15(5) — rank: law
Article 15 Cooperation of economic operators with market surveillance authorities. 5. Economic operators shall be able to present the information referred to in paragraph 3 for a period of six years after they have been supplied with the product, or with a part, a component or any software embedded into the product, or after they have supplied the product, as applicable.

[6] eu-reg-2024-1689, Recital 180 — rank: law
(180) The European Data Protection Supervisor and the European Data Protection Board were consulted in accordance with Article 42(1) and (2) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 and delivered their joint opinion on 18 June 2021,

[7] eu-dir-2012-18, Art. 29(1) — rank: law
Article 29 Reporting and review. 1. By 30 September 2020, and every four years thereafter, the Commission, on the basis of information submitted by Member States in accordance with Article 18 and Article 21(2) and of information held in databases, as referred to in Article 21(3) and (4), and taking into account the implementation of Article 4, shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report on the implementation and efficient functioning of this Directive, including information on major accidents that have occurred within the Union and their potential impact upon the implementation of this Directive. The Commission shall include in the first of those reports an assessment of the need to amend the scope of this Directive. Any report may, where appropriate, be accompanied by a legislative proposal.

[8] eu-dir-2012-18, Art. 21(5) — rank: law
Article 21 Information system and exchanges. 5. The Commission shall, by 1 January 2015, adopt implementing acts to establish the formats for communicating the information referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article from Member States and the relevant databases referred to in paragraphs 3 and 4. Those implementing acts shall be adopted in accordance with the examination procedure referred to in Article 27(2).

[9] eu-reg-2024-1689, Art. 113 — rank: law
Article 113 Entry into force and application This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 2 August 2026. However: (a) Chapters I and II shall apply from 2 February 2025; (b) Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101; (c) Article 6(1) and the corresponding obligations in this Regulation shall apply from 2 August 2027.

[10] eu-reg-2016-425, Art. 23 — rank: law
Article 23 Information obligation on notifying authorities Member States shall inform the Commission of their procedures for the assessment and notification of conformity assessment bodies and the monitoring of notified bodies, and of any changes thereto. The Commission shall make that information publicly available.

[11] eu-reg-2024-1689, Art. 50(5) — rank: law
Article 50 Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems. 5. The information referred to in paragraphs 1 to 4 shall be provided to the natural persons concerned in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure. The information shall conform to the applicable accessibility requirements.
